Flipkart says it has ‘robust governance’ as some staff face probe over alleged seller kickbacks
The employees allegedly exploited Flipkart’s B2B operations taking cuts from vendors in exchange for preferential treatment
By BL Bengaluru Bureau
Updated - October 31, 2026 at 08:57 PM.
×
Share
WhatsAppXFacebookLinkedInMessengerRedditMail
https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/flipkart-says-it-has-robust-governance-as-some-staff-face-probe-over-alleged-seller-kickbacks/article71650173.eceCopy
Walmart-owned e-commerce Flipkart noted that it has ‘robust governance processes and controls’ as the firm grapples with certain employees being investigated for allegedly receiving kickbacks for preferential treatment for some sales.
“Flipkart has robust governance processes and controls and is committed to the highest standards of integrity and compliance. We take any concerns seriously and address them through established processes. We remain committed to ensuring the highest standards of ethical conduct across our business,” said the company in its statement.
This comes after Flipkart had launched an investigation following whistleblower complaints alleging that employees in Flipkart’s smartphones and luggage and travel accessories (LTA) divisions received kickbacks.
Underway investigations
While the investigations are underway, the exact nature of the wrongdoings and the quantum is yet to be established.
The employees allegedly exploited Flipkart’s business-to-business (B2B) operations, taking cuts from vendors in exchange for preferential treatment, including greater visibility for sellers on the platform.
Shriram Subramanian, founder of corporate governance advisory firm InGovern, said financial controls and internal oversight mechanisms were important to prevent such practices, which were not uncommon across organisations.
An industry analyst, who did not wish to be named, said such instances could occur when certain dealers were more dependent on securing business than their competitors and were willing to offer incentives to employees to gain an advantage.
“This has happened earlier, and the company needs to fix the lapses,” the analyst said, adding that the employees involved could be at the mid- to senior-management level rather than the top leadership.
